cases.quote: The half em space overshoot or shortage is recovered by reducing inter-character spacing to a quarter em before the LEFT CORNER BRACKET and after the RIGHT CORNER BRACKET.
cases.rationale: §3.1.12's own worked figure (Figure 89) states two examples and not one, and this case and its sibling below are that structure at the geometry level rather than a reproduction of the figure's own twenty-character line: ② names a line that overshoots the aligned length by a half em because two punctuation marks fall together, ③ is the same line with inter-character spacing reduced to close exactly that overshoot; ④ names a line that cannot be repaired by reduction, and ⑤ is a character moved to the next line with the line it left behind expanded to close what moving the character opened up. Neither worked repair is a mechanism this case re-derives — `3.8.3/middle-dot-ideograph-middle-dot` and `D/two-differently-sized-middle-dots` already cover §3.8.3's own reduction procedure in full, and `3.8.4/dividing-punctuation-then-western` covers §3.8.4's expansion procedure the same way — so what this case adds is narrower than either: the two-example shape itself, one paragraph whose first repair is ③'s own kind and whose second is ⑤'s own kind, asserted at the line-geometry level §3.1.12 states one (predictable, aligned line lengths) and excuses the other (the paragraph's last line) from. This entry is the reduction repair: `first_line_indent` pushes the paragraph's own first line to end exactly at its first ideograph, forcing the second line onto its own remaining three items (a second ideograph, then two middle dots) with no candidate offered between them, 500 units over the shared measure — exactly the two middle dots' own combined reducible headroom (§D.2 note 1) plus the second ideograph's own boundary against the first middle dot — so `ladder::reduce` closes the whole 500-unit overshoot across the line's own four sites and the line reaches the measure exactly, the aligned length §3.1.12's own first item (①) states every non-last line keeps. This is the same fixture `crate::compose`'s own regression test composes (`a_second_lines_placements_are_shifted_by_the_reduction_the_ladder_applied`), reused here because it is already the minimal line whose overshoot spans more than one site the way ②/③'s own two-punctuation-mark line does, not because this case exists to re-verify that regression.

cases.quote: The opening bracket (cl-01) is moved to the second line, and line adjustment by inter-character spacing expansion is applied. That means that spacing is added in the first line at places where it is allowed.
cases.rationale: §3.1.12's own second worked example (④/⑤): a character that cannot stay on its own line — there, an opening bracket kinsoku forbids at the line end; here, the second line's own candidate simply is not offered any earlier — is moved to the following line, and the space its departure opens on the first is closed by expansion rather than left short. `？A亜` composed against a candidate only after the Western letter forces exactly this shape: the first line keeps `？A` and is 250 units short of `measure`, the second keeps the ideograph alone, and `ladder::expand` closes the first line's own 250-unit shortfall at Table 6's own second priority stage (the same site `3.8.4/dividing-punctuation-then-western` composes on its own terms) rather than leaving the line short of the aligned length ①'s own principle states. `Line::extent()` reaching `measure` on the first line and the second line's own single-item shortness — excused by §3.8.1's Note, which the first line's own is not — is the whole of what this entry asserts: the pull-up/push-down choice between competing breaks (§3.1.12 ⑤'s own second reading, `Line::pull_up`) is not asked here and is not asserted below: this paragraph offers exactly one candidate, so there is no second arrangement for `Search::Optimal` (M3) to compare it against, and `Line::pull_up` stays `None` for every line `Search::FirstFit` composes regardless (`jlreq_line::compose`'s own `Search::FirstFit` doc) — a fact about the search this milestone runs, not about either repair mechanism, and not this case's own distinguishing content, which is the two-example narrative itself.

cases.quote: Ideally, a full width spacing reduction would be applied, and the character "前" on the second line would be moved onto the first line in the 15th position. In that way, the problem could be avoided.
cases.rationale:
§3.1.12 ④ states the ideal repair in the same breath as the one it excuses: the sentence quoted above, before the text turns to why that repair is not taken in the worked figure ('a full-width spacing reduction is not possible') and ⑤'s push-down-then-expansion runs instead. The sibling case immediately above is built so the ideal repair is unavailable — one offered candidate, nothing to compare it against — and its own rationale states plainly that `Line::pull_up` stays `None` there under every search for that reason. This entry is the missing half: a paragraph where the ideal, reduction-based repair IS available, asked of `Search::Optimal` (`input.search`, the vocabulary this round adds) rather than `Search::FirstFit`, because `FirstFit` is the one search that never runs the comparison `Line::pull_up` reports the outcome of at all — it commits to one candidate per line before the ladder ever runs (`jlreq_line::compose::Search::FirstFit`'s own doc) — so no fixture, however available the ideal repair, would ever make it report one.

The paragraph ('？A亜亜・・', six items) offers four candidates, after every item but the first and last — an ordinary segmenter's own density, not a contrivance narrowing the search to the one break this case wants. At `measure = 2450` under `Search::Optimal { tolerance: 0 }` (the strict, non-neutral reading — `Search::Optimal`'s own doc names `Badness::WORST`, not `0`, as the neutral, most-permissive tolerance, and states that `Badness::ZERO` and every value short of `Badness::WORST` admit only a line the ladder can actually fit, so nothing here is reached through the tolerance-exhaustion fallback `docs/decisions/tolerance-exhaustion.md` publishes for a stricter caller-set floor), the nearer candidate — ending line 1 at '？A' alone — admits no complete arrangement of the paragraph at all: verified directly by composing this exact paragraph and measure with the farther candidate withheld (byte offset 7 removed, the other three kept), which collapses the search to its own single un-pruned pass and reports the whole six-item paragraph as one line, overfull by 2000 units, because '亜亜・・' — the four items that would remain after '？A' — needs more reduction to reach 2450 than its own four sites hold even fully drained (verified again, composed alone against the identical measure: still overfull by 550 once every site has reduced as far as it can). The farther candidate — ending line 1 at '？A亜' — is consequently the only offered break whose line closes at zero badness: reduction reclaims exactly the aligned length §3.1.12 ①'s own principle states every non-last line reaches, and the remaining '亜・・' reaches the identical 2450 units on its own account, short of nothing (badness zero either way, whether that reflects the same reduction or, as a line §3.8.1's Note would in any case excuse from expansion, being merely allowed to fall short — the geometry below states which, and neither reading changes what this case asserts).

`Search::Optimal` only ever chooses among `Feasible::compute`'s own admitted breaks and never a forbidden one (ADR-0010), so with exactly one admitted complete arrangement to report, it has none to prefer this one over — the discriminating test this round's own brief states in full: 'can you state, in prose, why JLReq's own words require this specific arrangement... without running the code?' Here the answer is that no other admitted arrangement exists, a fact about feasibility (§3.1.12 ①, §3.8's own ladder order, ADR-0010's admitted-break constraint) rather than about which of the two published `Question::ADJUSTMENT_PREFERENCE` readings — `least-adjustment` or `even-texture` — is in force; neither is named by this case's `policy: {}`, and neither would change the outcome, for that reason. `pull_up` is `Some` on line 1 because the nearer candidate (byte offset 4, the boundary before item 2) was genuinely a node the search scanned before it settled on the farther one (`pull_up_of`'s own first condition), and real reduction closed the farther choice's own gap (`pull_up_of`'s own second condition) — `pulls: 2` names item 2, the first of the two remaining ideographs, which would have opened line 2 under the nearer reading and sits on line 1 instead. `line[0].trims` is left unstated rather than asserted empty or populated: `conform --check`'s own `is_trim_rule` accepts only a bare §3.1.2 citation or a §B.1 (Table 1) cell, and this line's own reduction reports Appendix D.1's generic priority-stage citation instead — the identical address `3.8.3/middle-dot-ideograph-middle-dot`'s own case's reduction reports, and for the same reason, not re-derived here — so asserting the array would fail the very gate this case exists to pass; `placements`, `extent` and `pull_up.amount` already state the 250-unit geometry the trims would only restate.
